sentences.text: Estimates for the animal's size vary, with one calculation suggesting a length of 5.3 meters while another places it at 4.6 meters and a weight of 430 kilograms.

The holotype, which is the specimen the species is based on, includes the lower parts of the right thigh and shin bones from a young individual. These bones feature a prominent ridge on the inner side and uneven knee joints when viewed from the front.
This creature stands out as one of the most recent non-bird theropods known from the Patagonia region.
Rodolfo Coria formally named the genus in 2001 after finding fossils at a site called Salitral Ojo de Agua in the Neuquén Basin of Argentina.
Scientists can only study the leg bones, which resemble those of other abelisaurids but lack unique features that would clearly define the group.
The environment was likely a wet coastal area where dense forests of palms and cypress pines grew near swamps and shallow lagoons.
It belongs to the theropod family Abelisauridae and is part of the clade Furileusauria, which links it more closely to Carnotaurus than to other relatives.
The animal lived in what is now South America during the Upper Cretaceous, specifically between the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages, roughly 75 million years ago.
Some researchers argue the name is invalid because no single trait is unique to the animal, noting that similar ridges and shin bone shapes appear in other genera like Aucasaurus and Rajasaurus.
Additionally, the classification of the subfamily Carnotaurinae remains uncertain, with different studies including or excluding various related species.
